goal: Reduce representative warm codex-core verification from more than 30 minutes to at most 10 minutes, with a stretch target of 5 minutes, while retaining a slower release-equivalent gate.

lowVsHighReleaseDifference.interpretation: Equivalent within run noise; crate-level codex-core invalidation, not symbol-level fanout, controls the release rebuild.

feasibility.basis: Targeted changed-core check took 37.45s and broad workspace check took 338.829s; warm optimized executable build took 1845.745s.

rootCauseRanking.cause: Crate-granular optimized rebuild through codex-core's 25-package consumer surface.
rootCauseRanking.evidence: A private one-line edit rebuilt 25 package IDs with 0 hits, 25 misses, and 30:45.745 wall time.

rootCauseRanking.cause: A release executable build is used as a generic per-edit verification gate.
rootCauseRanking.evidence: The same edit passed targeted check in 37.45s; a high-fanout workspace check passed in 5:38.829.

rootCauseRanking.cause: Fresh worktree-local release targets and cold exact fingerprints add the native and full dependency graph.
rootCauseRanking.evidence: Cold/current-fingerprint iteration build took 50:50.418; aws-lc-sys build script alone took 466.03s.

rootCauseRanking.cause: sccache cannot reuse changed codex-core or unchanged consumers compiled against a different core artifact.
rootCauseRanking.evidence: Warm private edit had zero hits and 25 misses while all cache error counters remained zero.
Historical direct measurement: 58:05, 939 crates, zero sccache requests.

candidateDirections.name: Canonical measured tiered verifier
candidateDirections.summary: Make targeted check the default edit loop, workspace check the hard integration gate, and executable/publish builds explicit slower tiers.
why: Directly meets both verification thresholds on current code and toolchain.
Preserves stronger workspace, scoped-test, executable, and release gates.
Uses wrapper scripts and documentation rather than upstream-canonical Rust changes.
Adds timing and cache observability so later regressions are measurable.

candidateDirections.name: Separate incremental fast-runnable lane
candidateDirections.summary: If a runnable binary itself must be at most 10 minutes, A/B the existing dev-small profile with incremental enabled, no sccache, and a separate target directory.
whyNotFirst: Requires an expensive cold warm-up and another large target directory.
Not needed to meet the stated verification target.

candidateDirections.name: Stabilize or split codex-core consumer boundaries
candidateDirections.summary: Reduce release invalidation only if a runnable binary must meet the target and the lower-conflict incremental experiment fails.
whyNotFirst: A useful split must narrow consumer dependencies; merely extracting a leaf wrapped by codex-core will not help.
Highest upstream rebase and conflict surface.
Check-based verification already meets the target.

tieredVerificationContract.name: integration / Phase 5a
tieredVerificationContract.command: cargo check --workspace --timings plus scoped tests for touched crates

tieredVerificationContract.name: runnable behavior
tieredVerificationContract.command: frozen LTO-off cargo build --release -p codex-cli --bin codex-core
tieredVerificationContract.rule: Explicit only; never an implicit consequence of T1 or T2.

tieredVerificationContract.name: release equivalent
tieredVerificationContract.command: existing thin-LTO, no-sccache publish command and runtime smoke
tieredVerificationContract.rule: Retained unchanged and allowed to be slow.

conflictSurface: Serialize changes to scripts/iteration-env.sh and scripts/measure-build.ps1 with other build-perf work.
Update CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.override.md together because they duplicate the verification hierarchy.
Do not change codex-rs source, Cargo features, release profile, or crate boundaries in the first implementation.
Do not default to one globally shared Cargo target while concurrent worktrees are normal.
acceptanceThresholds: Warm private codex-core edit passes T1 in at most 5 minutes, with a hard ceiling of 10 minutes.
High-fanout public codex-core edit passes T2 in at most 10 minutes.
T1 no-op completes in at most 30 seconds and invokes no rustc.
T1 and T2 record command, SHA, target, toolchain, profile, linker, and sccache health.
T3 is explicit and T4 remains the existing release-equivalent gate.
Repeated iteration-env sourcing does not restart sccache solely because its displayed Windows path is escaped.
A cache wipe requires a reproducible cache error, not a cold fingerprint.
The first implementation changes no upstream-canonical Rust source.

planSeed.goal: Operationalize sub-10-minute codex-core verification without weakening final gates.
stories: Generalize scripts/measure-build.ps1 for core check, workspace check, and iteration build.
Add scripts/verify-core-change.sh with explicit T1/T2/T3 dispatch and non-escalating defaults.
Normalize sccache Windows paths in scripts/iteration-env.sh and dogfood repeated sourcing.
Update rebase, publish, CLAUDE/AGENTS, and build-perf documentation in one synchronized change.
Re-run the low/high probes through the final command and retain compact evidence.
Rewrite or archive the stale unconditional build-env-sccache-cache-wipe-and-rewarm task.
File a separate fast-runnable profile experiment only if runnable output must meet 10 minutes.

remainingMeasurements: Current exact thin-LTO/no-sccache publish build in a separate target; historical 58:05 evidence already establishes that it is a slow release-only gate.
Separate-target dev-small/incremental warm low/high A/B if a runnable binary must meet 10 minutes.
Remote sccache seeding only if cross-machine cold exact-fingerprint builds recur often enough to justify it.
